$comment: RAAST Spanish (es) LTR host profile. Spanish is the first left-to-right host: the page runs LTR while embedding Arabic/Hebrew content (refugee services, heritage sites, i18n demos). The engine flips: instead of isolating LTR atoms inside RTL prose, it requires RTL runs inside Spanish prose to be isolated, checks inverted marks, and never suggests dir=rtl on <html>.
name: Spanish

numerals.thousands_separator_note: es-ES uses period thousands (1.234.567) or thin space; most LatAm locales invert separators (1,234,567.89). Pick per project locale and stay consistent.
numerals.percent_placement: es-ES: space before (25 %); LatAm: attached (25%) — follow project locale

punctuation.inverted_marks_note: RAE requires opening ¿ and ¡ on questions and exclamations in prose. Missing inverted marks are the most visible machine-generated-Spanish defect.
punctuation.quotes_note: RAE prefers «comillas angulares» in prose; curly quotes are acceptable in UI copy.

letters.script_note: Latin alphabet with ñ and accented vowels (á é í ó ú ü) — any shipped font must cover Latin-1 plus ¿ ¡ « » or glyphs fall back inconsistently.

currency.name: euro
currency.placement: after amount, non-breaking space per RAE: 25 €

bidi_marks.notes: LTR host: Arabic/Hebrew names, quotes and snippets inside Spanish prose MUST be wrapped in <bdi> or dir="rtl" — bare RTL runs visually reorder surrounding punctuation and numbers (the #1 bidi defect in es pages serving RTL content).
